'''Vera G. Lüth''' (born 1943) is an experimental [[Particle physics|particle physicist]] and professor emerita at [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] (SLAC), [[Stanford University]], in the United States. A senator of the [[Helmholtz Association of German Research Centres|Helmholtz Association]], she has worked in particle physics at SLAC since 1974. She is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].

== Early life and education ==
Lüth completed her undergraduate education at [[University of Mainz|Mainz University]] Institute of Physics from 1963 to 1966. In 1969 she completed a [[Master of Science]] in physics at [[Heidelberg University]]; her [[Dr. rer. nat.]] work in particle physics was also completed there from 1966 to 1974, based on research at CERN.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://inspirehep.net/author/profile/V.Luth.1|title=Lüth, Vera G. – Profile – INSPIRE-HEP|website=inspirehep.net|access-date=2016-07-17}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite thesis|type=PhD|last=Vera|first=Luth|date=1974|title=Measurement of the Charge Asymmetry in the Decay K0 --&gt; pi+- e-+ Neutrino as a Function of the K0 Decay Time|url=http://inspirehep.net/record/89948?ln=en|publisher=[[Heidelberg University]]|language=en}}</ref> Her 1974 dissertation, titled ''Measurement of the Charge Asymmetry in the Decay K0 --> pi+- e-+ Neutrino as a Function of the K0 Decay Time,''<ref name=":4" /> was advised by [[Jack Steinberger|Jack H. Steinberger]] and Heinz August Adolf Wilhelm Filthuth.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/physics/tree.php?pid=595135&fontsize=1&pnodecount=4&cnodecount=2|title=Physics Tree – Vera Luth Family Tree|website=academictree.org|access-date=2017-02-17}}</ref>

In 1977 she married Karl L. Brown (1925–2002) in Santa Clara County, California.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.crystal-reflections.com/sites/karl_brown/obituary.html|title=Karl Leslie Brown – Obituary|website=www.crystal-reflections.com|access-date=2016-07-17}}</ref>

== Career ==
Lüth was hired at [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|SLAC]] as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] from 1974 to 1984.<ref name=":2" />

She returned to [[CERN]] as a scientific associate from 1984 to 1985, working with Jack Steinberger and others to measure [[CP violation|charge-parity violation]] in neutral [[kaon]] decay.<ref name=":1" /> By 1984, Lüth had joined the permanent faculty at SLAC. Between 1992 and 1994, she was deputy associate director of research at the [[Superconducting Super Collider]] (SSC) laboratory in Texas.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2016|title=Prof. Dr Vera Luth|url=https://www.helmholtz.de/en/about_us/the_association/statutes_and_governance/senate_and_senate_commission/members_of_the_senate/prof_dr_vera_lueth/|access-date=2016-07-17|website=Helmholtz Association|publisher=}}</ref> When construction of the SSC was cancelled, she returned to SLAC as the first technical coordinator for the [[BaBar experiment|BaBar]] detector, with responsibilities for overseeing the detector's design and construction. Upon its completion, she turned her efforts to measuring decay of [[B meson|''B'' mesons]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://today.slac.stanford.edu/feature/2010/luth-symposium.asp|title=Symposium Honors Vera Lüth|last=|first=|date=|website=SLAC Today|publisher=SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Menlo Park, California|access-date=2016-07-17}}</ref> According to Kelen Tuttle, writing for ''SLAC Today'', "Lüth was one of the leading physicists on both the magnetic detector built by SLAC and [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] and the MARK II detector, which recorded data at [[SPEAR]], the Positron Electron Project and the Stanford Linear Collider. Lüth was also the driving force to build the first detector using silicon microstrips at a colliding beam machine."<ref name=":1" />

In 2004 she was promoted to Professor of Research at SLAC.<ref name=":0" />

Lüth served as a permanent member of the Helmholtz Association's Senate Commission from 2008 to 2011, and in 2011she was appointed a senator of the [[Helmholtz Association of German Research Centres|Helmholtz Association]] for the research field of the structure of matter.<ref name=":0" /> She has participated on numerous advisory committees and panels, including the German [[German Council of Science and Humanities|Wissenschaftsrat's]] Large Facilities Panel, and the [[United States Department of Energy|Department of Energy]] and [[National Science Foundation]] [[High Energy Physics Advisory Panel]].<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
Lüth has conducted research at [[CERN]] in Switzerland, Heidelberg University in Germany, and SLAC. According to SLAC theoretical physicist [[JoAnne L. Hewett|JoAnne Hewett]], "Right from the beginning, Vera showed that every experiment she contributed to was the definitive experiment at the time."<ref name=":1" /> [[Burton Richter]] said she proved her worth early, "playing an important role at the Stanford Positron Electron Accelerating Ring (SPEAR) during the '[[J/psi meson|November Revolution]],' which launched a new era of particle physics with the discovery of the [[charm quark]]".<ref name=":1" /> Her research interests have included [[Symmetry in quantum mechanics|fundamental symmetries]], heavy flavor particle [[Weak interaction|weak decays]], silicon vertex detectors, and precision tracking.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ppa.slac.stanford.edu/ppa-emeriti-bios|title=PPA Emeriti Bios|date=2014-12-15|access-date=2016-07-18|archive-date=June 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170611005701/https://ppa.slac.stanford.edu/ppa-emeriti-bios|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In addition to co-authoring more than 700 publications on particle physics,<ref name=":2" /> Luth has contributed a historical biography of [[Wolfgang K. H. Panofsky]] to the ''[[Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lüth|first=Vera G.|date=2013-01-01|title=Wolfgang K.H. Panofsky: Scientist and Arms-Control Expert|journal=[[Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science]]|volume=63|issue=1|pages=1–20|doi=10.1146/annurev-nucl-102711-095043|doi-access=free|bibcode=2013ARNPS..63....1L}}</ref>

== Honors ==
Lüth was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1984, and cited "For Contributions to the discovery of new particles and to the determination of their properties."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=L&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org|access-date=2016-07-21}}</ref>

She was honored as [[Emeritus|professor emerita]] at SLAC in 2010.<ref name=":1" />
